usecases.title: Set up a project from approved master data
usecases.story: A project manager sets up a newly approved IT project: its name, business unit, portfolio, the department head and sponsor who oversee it, its contract and purchase-order details, its approved budget and contingency, and who is on the team. The form insists on the key details before it will save, and once saved the project is the single record that schedules, costs and status reports all build on. People who are not on the project, and roles with no business seeing project set-up, are kept out.

usecases.title: Build and baseline the project schedule
usecases.story: A project manager builds the project schedule: adds activities with planned dates, links them by dependency, marks milestones, and locks in an approved baseline that later progress is measured against. The system keeps the baseline fixed and records schedule history, and people outside the project team cannot alter the schedule.

usecases.title: Assign and reassign activities to team members
usecases.story: A project manager hands each activity to a team member and can move it to someone else later. The new owner is told, the change is traceable, and each team member can narrow the schedule down to just their own work.

usecases.title: Track progress, actuals and forecast during the period
usecases.story: While work is under way, team members record how far along their activities are and the actual start and finish dates, and the project manager updates forecast dates. The system works out whether each activity is on track, and warns the owner when the forecast slips past the approved baseline.

usecases.title: Manage issues, action items and decisions
usecases.story: A project manager logs a problem as an issue with a category, priority, owner and target date, breaks it into action items with owners, records the decisions taken, and watches overdue items. Critical or long-overdue issues escalate by themselves so the steering committee sees them, and action items past their due date flip to overdue on their own.

usecases.title: Manage the project risk register
usecases.story: A project manager keeps the risk register: records each risk, rates its likelihood and impact, assigns an owner and a response plan, and tracks it over time. The overall rating follows the agreed five-by-five scale automatically, and high or critical risks are flagged to the risk owner.

usecases.title: Manage project financials
usecases.story: A project manager records what has actually been spent, what is committed and what is forecast, including invoices, against the project budget. The totals add up on their own and budget changes and contingency draw-downs are visible against the approved figures.

usecases.title: Generate, preview and submit the monthly PSR
usecases.story: At month end the project manager prepares the monthly status report from live project data, previews it, and submits it. The form insists on the project, the narrative update and the reporting month before it will go forward. Once submitted it lands with the project's department head, who is told it is waiting, and a reminder goes out as the deadline nears.

usecases.title: Revise and resubmit a returned PSR
usecases.story: When a reviewer sends a status report back with a comment, it returns to the project manager with everything they entered still intact. The manager is told why, fixes it and resubmits, and it goes back through review from the start.

usecases.title: Monitor schedule performance via the S-curve
usecases.story: A project manager looks at the cumulative planned, actual and forecast progress curve for a project, with the schedule performance figures and a table view of the same numbers.

usecases.title: Work my assigned tasks (My Tasks)
usecases.story: A team member opens their personal task list and sees only the activities and action items assigned to them across their projects, is told when something new is assigned, and updates their own progress. They cannot see or change other people's work or anything financial.

usecases.title: Review and approve/return a PSR
usecases.story: A department head is told a status report is waiting, reviews it and either approves it or sends it back with a comment. When approved, the system decides whether the project's sponsor also has to sign off (for example when the project is red) or whether the report can be finalised straight away.

usecases.title: Approve a PSR requiring Sponsor sign-off
usecases.story: A project sponsor is told a department-head-approved report needs their sign-off, reviews it, and either approves it, which locks the report, or sends it back with a comment.

usecases.title: Monitor portfolio health and identify projects needing attention
usecases.story: A member of the steering committee sees every project in the portfolio, filters by status, health, risk and business unit, and spots the projects needing attention. They can look at everything but are not allowed to change project data.

usecases.title: Generate the Portfolio PSR (PPSR) and view PSR history
usecases.story: A steering committee member builds the consolidated portfolio status report from the approved project reports and looks back through earlier reports and their approval status over time.

usecases.title: Configure the working calendar and alert settings
usecases.story: The hub administrator maintains the working calendar of holidays and non-working days and sets the alert thresholds, reminder periods and recipients. Nobody else can change these settings.

usecases.title: Administer users, roles and project access
usecases.story: The hub administrator creates user accounts, puts people into roles, switches access on and off, and assigns people to the projects they should see, so that each person only sees what they are allowed to.

usecases.title: Review the audit trail
usecases.story: The hub administrator reviews the audit trail of what was done by whom, and can trace one status report from creation through submission, approval or return, with comments and timestamps.

tests.title: Journey: Set up a project from approved master data

PM creates the project record: code, name, business unit, portfolio, assigned DH/PS.
PM records the procurement/contract details: vendor, NOA/PO/NTP dates, contract value, expiry.
PM records the approved budget and the approved contingency fund.
PM sets up the initial project team (who is assigned to this project).
asserts: Every step completes without a permission or validation error
Outcome holds: The project exists as the single source of truth that scheduling, financials and later PSRs all build on.
Success criterion observed: Project appears correctly in the portfolio list (ITPH-00124)
Success criterion observed: Changes to approved master data flow through to later PSRs and project records automatically (BR-13)

tests.title: Journey: Build and baseline the project schedule
steps: Sign in as the journey's role (acceptance sandbox user).
PM creates, edits and deletes project activities.
PM defines planned start/end dates for each activity.
PM defines dependencies between activities.
PM identifies and maintains project milestones.
PM establishes the approved schedule baseline.
PM generates and views the Gantt chart.
asserts: Every step completes without a permission or validation error
Outcome holds: An approved, dependency-consistent schedule with a locked baseline that later progress is measured against.
Success criterion observed: A baseline is established and stays fixed once approved (BRD §1.4 'Baseline' definition)
Success criterion observed: Every change to the schedule is captured in schedule history (ITPH-0014)

tests.title: Journey: Assign and reassign activities to team members
steps: Sign in as the journey's role (acceptance sandbox user).
PM assigns each activity and milestone to a responsible team member.
The assignee is notified.
PM reassigns an activity to another team member at any time; the change is recorded in schedule history.
PM (or team member) filters the schedule to just their own assigned activities.
asserts: Every step completes without a permission or validation error
Outcome holds: Every activity has a single clear owner, and every reassignment is traceable.
Success criterion observed: Every open activity has an assignee
Success criterion observed: Reassignments are visible in schedule history, not silently overwritten

tests.title: Journey: Track progress, actuals and forecast during the period
steps: Sign in as the journey's role (acceptance sandbox user).
Assignees record % complete, actual start and actual finish for their own activities.
PM manually updates forecast start/finish dates when their assessment of progress changes.
PM views planned vs. actual schedules to spot variance.
PM is alerted when the forecast finish passes the baseline finish or a schedule-risk threshold.
asserts: Every step completes without a permission or validation error
Outcome holds: The schedule reflects true current status, with schedule health computed and an early warning raised on slippage.
Success criterion observed: Schedule health (Green/Amber/Red) is computed per BR-03
Success criterion observed: An alert fires the moment forecast finish exceeds baseline finish

tests.title: Journey: Manage issues, action items and decisions
steps: Sign in as the journey's role (acceptance sandbox user).

PM assigns an issue owner and a target resolution date.
PM records the actions required to resolve the issue and assigns action items to team members.
PM tracks action item status so overdue actions are visible.
PM records project decisions and their rationale.
The issue escalates automatically when Critical or overdue past the configured aging period.
asserts: Every step completes without a permission or validation error
Outcome holds: Issues are tracked to resolution or escalated, with owners and action items clearly assigned.
Success criterion observed: Critical or aged-overdue issues escalate and appear on the PSC view (ITPH-0040, BR-21)
Success criterion observed: Every action item has a status and an owner

tests.title: Journey: Manage the project risk register
steps: Sign in as the journey's role (acceptance sandbox user).

PM categorizes the risk.
PM assesses probability and impact; the overall risk rating is computed per BR-04.
PM assigns a risk owner.
PM defines mitigation actions and a response strategy.
PM monitors residual risk after mitigation.
The risk escalates automatically when rated High or Critical.
PM maintains risk history/status over time.
asserts: Every step completes without a permission or validation error
Outcome holds: Every risk has a current rating, an owner and a mitigation plan; High/Critical risks are visible to governance.
Success criterion observed: Risk rating always follows the 5x5 probability x impact matrix (BR-04)
Success criterion observed: High/Critical risks appear on the PSC view (ITPH-0049)

PM compares approved budget, actual cost, committed cost and forecast cost to spot variances; views the remaining budget/forecast balance.
asserts: Every step completes without a permission or validation error

Success criterion observed: Budget vs actual vs committed vs forecast reconciles for the PSR (ITPH-0068, 0069)
Success criterion observed: Cost health (Green/Amber/Red) is computed per BR-05

tests.title: Journey: Generate, preview and submit the monthly PSR
steps: Sign in as the journey's role (acceptance sandbox user).
The Hub reminds the PM before the deadline.
PM generates the PSR; static and computed sections (schedule, milestone, issue, risk, financial, action data) auto-populate from live data.
PM adds a narrative update and defines/confirms the reporting period.
PM attaches supporting documents.
PM identifies activities behind/ahead of schedule and milestones missed or forecast to be missed, and plans the next period's activities/milestones.
PM previews the PSR before submission and submits it to the DH.
asserts: Every step completes without a permission or validation error
Outcome holds: A complete, accurate PSR -- built from system data, not re-typed -- submitted for approval on time.
Success criterion observed: PSR is submitted by the working-day-5 deadline (BR-11)
Success criterion observed: Auto-populated static fields match approved project master data and are never edited on an approved PSR (BR-13)

tests.title: Journey: Monitor schedule performance via the S-curve
steps: Sign in as the journey's role (acceptance sandbox user).
PM views the cumulative planned vs actual vs forecast S-curve for the project.
PM sees planned % to date, actual % to date, variance in percentage points and SPI.
PM hovers over the curve for exact weekly values, or views the same data as a table.
The S-curve is included when the PSR is generated.
asserts: Every step completes without a permission or validation error
Outcome holds: Schedule performance trend is visible at a glance, quantified with SPI, and carried into the PSR.
Success criterion observed: S-curve points are computed per BR-17 (weekly, weighted by activity duration, planned from baseline / actual from actuals / forecast from today to forecast finish)

tests.title: Journey: Work my assigned tasks (My Tasks)
steps: Sign in as the journey's role (acceptance sandbox user).
I receive a notification that an activity has been assigned to me.
I see it on my My Tasks page, alongside every other open activity and action item assigned to me across all my projects, with status and due dates.
I update % complete, actual start and actual finish for MY OWN activities only.
If I try to edit an activity that is not assigned to me, I am blocked.
I can filter the schedule view to show only my own assigned activities.
asserts: Every step completes without a permission or validation error
Outcome holds: My work is visible and updatable from one place, without my being able to touch anyone else's schedule items.
Success criterion observed: Entering % complete > 0 sets the actual start if blank; entering 100% sets the actual finish to today (BR-15)
Success criterion observed: An assignee can never edit an activity not assigned to them (BR-15, ITPH-00257)

tests.title: Journey: Review and approve/return a PSR
steps: Sign in as the journey's role (acceptance sandbox user).
DH is notified that a PSR requires approval.
DH reviews the submitted PSR's schedule, issue, risk, financial and action content.
DH approves the PSR, or returns it with mandatory comments.
If approved, the system checks the PS routing rule (BR-10) and either routes the PSR to the PS or finalizes it.
DH can view the PSR's approval status and full history at any time.
asserts: Every step completes without a permission or validation error
Outcome holds: Only validated PSRs advance; every return carries an actionable, recorded comment.
Success criterion observed: No PSR advances to Approved without an explicit DH action
Success criterion observed: A returned PSR always carries a comment (BR-25)

tests.title: Journey: Approve a PSR requiring Sponsor sign-off
steps: Sign in as the journey's role (acceptance sandbox user).
PS is notified of a PSR pending approval.
PS reviews the DH-approved PSR.
PS approves or returns the PSR.
asserts: Every step completes without a permission or validation error
Outcome holds: The PSR receives the Bank's full governance sign-off, or is sent back for correction, per the routing rule.
Success criterion observed: PS only ever sees PSRs that actually meet BR-10's routing conditions

PSC filters projects by status, health, risk, business unit and other criteria.
PSC views dashboards of project status, risk, issue, milestone and financial performance.

PSC views critical issues and overdue actions, and high/critical risks.
asserts: Every step completes without a permission or validation error
Outcome holds: The PSC directs its attention to the projects that need it, without requesting ad-hoc reports.
Success criterion observed: 'Needs management attention' is computed consistently per BR-06 (overall Red, or any Critical risk/issue, or any overdue escalation)

tests.title: Journey: Generate the Portfolio PSR (PPSR) and view PSR history
steps: Sign in as the journey's role (acceptance sandbox user).
PSC views consolidated project status information across the portfolio.
PSC generates the Portfolio Project Status Report (PPSR).
PSC (and PM) view historical PSRs to review performance and status trends over time.
PSC views the approval status of PSRs across the portfolio.
asserts: Every step completes without a permission or validation error
Outcome holds: A consolidated, board-ready portfolio status report and a browsable PSR history.
Success criterion observed: The PPSR only rolls up PSRs that have reached Approved (locked snapshot), per BR-24

tests.title: Journey: Configure the working calendar and alert settings
steps: Sign in as the journey's role (acceptance sandbox user).
Admin adds, edits or removes holidays and special non-working days, including dates and coverage.
Admin configures alert thresholds, contract-expiration notification periods, aging periods and recipients for reminders and escalations.
asserts: Every step completes without a permission or validation error
Outcome holds: Schedule calculations (working-day logic) and escalation/reminder timing reflect current Bank policy without any code change.
Success criterion observed: Working-day-dependent calculations (durations, dependencies, forecasts, PSR deadline) respect the configured calendar (BR-01)

tests.title: Journey: Administer users, roles and project access
steps: Sign in as the journey's role (acceptance sandbox user).
Admin creates and maintains user accounts.
Admin assigns users to appropriate roles.
Admin activates, deactivates or modifies user access.
Admin assigns users to specific projects, so each user can access only the projects relevant to their responsibilities; access defaults to deny-all otherwise.
Admin maintains role permissions centrally.
asserts: Every step completes without a permission or validation error
Outcome holds: Every user's access matches their current responsibility and their current project assignments; no orphaned or over-privileged accounts.
Success criterion observed: A user with no project assignment sees no project data (BR-23)

tests.title: Journey: Review the audit trail
steps: Sign in as the journey's role (acceptance sandbox user).
Admin views all system transactions and user actions recorded in the audit trail.
Admin (or any authorized user) traces a specific PSR's full lifecycle history -- creation, modification, submission, approval, return, comments, responsible users, timestamps.
asserts: Every step completes without a permission or validation error
Outcome holds: Any change to project data, reports, approvals, configuration or access can be traced to the responsible user.

Success criterion observed: Every one of the confirmed audit log event types is captured (open question: the exact '7 identified log events' of ITPH-00213 are unconfirmed by LANDBANK -- see open-questions.md)
